subject: Capacity reconciliation & closing invoice for Q1 overages
messages:
From: Claire Moss <claire.moss@scalefab.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Question about Q1 capacity charges

Hi Lauren,

We just received the April invoice and noticed an unexpected one-time charge labeled 'Q1 usage reconciliation'. Our finance team says the amount doesn't match the usage report we have. Can you help me understand what triggered the charge and share the detailed usage breakdown?

I attached the PDF they sent, but if you can point us to the underlying token/instance-level detail that would be ideal — we need to reconcile before our April close.

Thanks,
Claire Moss
Director of Finance
Scalefab Inc.
[Attachment: invoice_april.pdf]
From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Moss <claire.moss@scalefab.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question about Q1 capacity charges

Hi Claire — thanks for flagging this. I pulled the billing details and it looks like two things happened: a sustained burst in peak throughput on 2027-02-27 (long-running batch inference) that exceeded their Dedicated capacity buffer, and a late-posted usage export from the customer's internal job scheduler that we received on 2027-03-15. Together those triggered the one-time reconciliation charge.

I attached the raw usage CSV we generated and a draft one-off invoice that aligns with our internal reconciliation. I'm copying Ben from Finance to confirm the math and propose options (credit vs amortized top-up).

Attachment: scalefab_q1_usage.csv, oneoff_invoice_98721.pdf

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
Direct: +1 415 555 0123
From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question about Q1 capacity charges

Thanks — reviewed the CSV. The raw numbers line up with the invoice, but there are two levers to make this easier for Scalefab: (1) apply a one-time goodwill credit to soften the hit (we often do 10-20% on first-time post-renewal spikes) and (2) offer a short-term capacity top-up (60-day add-on) they can prepay that we'll credit against the invoice.

If we go with (2) we need a signed MOU for the top-up and a PO or signed invoice. I've drafted language for the MOU (see attachment). If Lauren is comfortable proposing a blended option to Claire (40% credit + top-up), I can prepare the revised invoice and mark it with the deal id DL-98721 for easy tracking.

Attachment: signed-mou-topup.pdf (draft)
From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Moss <claire.moss@scalefab.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@scalefab.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question about Q1 capacity charges

Claire / Tom — quick update from our side after an internal review. Short summary: the charge is a reconciliation for ~3.2M extra tokens consumed outside your reserved pool in Q1. Ben in Finance recommends a blended accommodation: a one-time 35% credit off the reconciliation invoice plus a 60-day capacity top-up (same SKU, pre-paid) that we will apply to future usage.

If that works for you we can:
- Issue a revised invoice reflecting the 35% credit (net amount = $28,950)
- Provision the 60-day top-up immediately after we receive the PO (or a signed MOU) and mark the top-up amount as a credit against the invoice
- Provide a detailed token-level export showing daily peak statistics for your internal audit

Next step: can you confirm whether Scalefab prefers a PO (our usual path) or DocuSign for the MOU? If PO, send to billing@redwood.ai and we'll route for immediate provisioning.

Thanks — I know month-end is tight.

—Lauren
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Claire Moss <claire.moss@scalefab.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@scalefab.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question about Q1 capacity charges

Lauren — thanks for the clear breakdown and the credit proposal. We ran this by procurement and legal this morning. They are happy to accept the blended option (35% credit + 60-day top-up) but procurement prefers to use a PO referencing the revised invoice rather than DocuSign.

Action items on our side: procurement will issue PO #SF-2027-04-059 and attach the signed MOU note. Expect the PO to hit billing@redwood.ai within two business days. Can you confirm the net amount and the account reference we should expect on the PO?

Thanks,
Claire
From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Moss <claire.moss@scalefab.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@scalefab.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2027 15:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question about Q1 capacity charges

Great — appreciate the quick turnaround. Net amounts and references below for the PO:

- Original reconciliation amount (pre-credit): $44,538.00
- Agreed credit: 35% ($15,588.30)
- Net amount due (revised invoice): $28,949.70 -> rounded on invoice to $28,950.00
- PO reference: Scalefab Inc. / DL-98721 / PO SF-2027-04-059
- Send PO to: billing@redwood.ai

I'll ask Finance to prepare the revised invoice PDF and provision the 60-day top-up on receipt of the PO. Once the PO and MOU are attached we'll mark the case resolved and send the signed MOU back for your records.

Final note for internal tracking: Rachel — please hold the top-up SKU so we can provision immediately on PO receipt and apply the credit against invoice DL-98721. Ben — when you close the invoice, flag it in HubSpot under deal DL-98721.

Thanks all — will update when the PO lands.

—Lauren
